 ORDER

Date : 04-11-2019

 Heard Mr. J. Sharma, learned counsel for the appellant.

Page No.# 2/2

 Issue notice on the respondent by registered post with A/D, returnable by 4 (four) weeks.

The petition under Section 10(1)(x) read with Section 15 of the Divorce Act, 1989 was preferred
by the appellant herein for a dissolution of a marriage with the respondent. By the Order of
14.09.2018, the learned Principal Judge, Family Court No. 1, Kamrup arrived at a conclusion that the
appellant is a Hindu by birth and religion, whereas, the respondent is a Christian by birth and religion
belonging to the Scheduled Caste community and therefore, they could not have solemnized their
marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act . By referring to section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, it
was taken note of that a marriage may be solemnized under the Act between only two Hindus and
therefore a marriage solemnized under the Hindu rites and rituals between one Hindu and one
Christian cannot be treated as a valid married, and accordingly the petition stood disallowed.
